## 1. Expansion thesis

This plan expands attention around six chairs and one memory while leaving the journal row intact. Its center is six folding chairs around a table and one person who remembers. The bank tests different distances and registers for rereading the same recorded material; it does not add a new day, memory, event, relationship, quest, or system.

## 2. Story question

What makes a chapel when its book is gone, no one comes, and its keeper cannot check memory against another standard?

## 3. Verified source record

The complete JSON entry below is copied from the current local source. Preserve its id, author_id, author_name, day, hour, knowledge_key, timestamp, and exact text. Candidate prose is editorial material, not part of the loaded row.

```json
{
  "id": "journal_raw_b3_09_priest_the_empty_chapel",
  "text": "No one came to the chapel this week. Not for the Wednesday gathering, not for the Sunday quiet hour. The chapel is a store room we cleared of crates and filled with six folding chairs and a table I call an altar because it is the table we put things on when we need a table to put things on. I do not have a book. I had a book. It was water-damaged and the pages stuck and I could not turn them without tearing. I tore out the pages I could still read and I read them until I had read them and then I had nothing left to read. I speak now from what I remember. I am not certain I remember it correctly. The Watchmaker says memory is a mechanism that drifts and must be calibrated against an external standard. I do not have an external standard. I have what I remember. I sat in the chapel alone for an hour. Six chairs and a table and one person who remembers. That is enough for a chapel. It has to be.",
  "timestamp": "Day 142, 19h",
  "author_name": "The Priest",
  "author_id": "the_priest",
  "knowledge_key": "priest_no_attendance_drift",
  "day": 142,
  "hour": 19.0
}
```

## 4. Fixed canon and open space

No one attends the Wednesday gathering or Sunday quiet hour. The cleared storeroom has six folding chairs and a table called an altar; the Priest’s water-damaged book was torn apart, and he now speaks from memory while doubting its accuracy. The Watchmaker compares memory to a drifting mechanism. Do not supply doctrine, a congregation, or a recovered book. Candidate language may add an image, rhythm, or private impression as an editorial draft, but no proposed addition becomes a further remembered event or a confirmed fact until the existing content owner selects and reviews it against the source.

## 5. Human center

The source voice is The Priest. The Priest’s voice is earnest but self-questioning, finding a modest definition of a chapel without claiming certainty about remembered pages. Let the six chairs and the one person remain ordinary facts before they become symbols. The prose may notice what the author can count, hear, repair, fear, or leave uncertain, while keeping the account’s limits visible.
